overrides.adjustmentNote: Atlas replaces the legacy Luna rating 3/3/0/3 with Discraft's current Hard Luna numbers, 3/4/0/2: glide 3 to 4, fade 3 to 2, speed 3 and turn 0 unchanged. Marshall Street explains that Luna was renumbered when the more overstable Kratos took over 3/3/0/3; the Luna mold did not change. Infinite Discs lists manufacturer numbers 3/4/0/2 and reviewer-average numbers 3/3.2/-0.2/2 (139 ratings). Marshall Street's current Z Swirl Luna listing also gives fade 2. Independent reviews by Disc Golf Puttheads and Disc Golf Reviewer both describe less fade than the old 3 rating, rather than exact agreement on every number. Atlas previously stacked Luna and Kratos at the same rating anchor (both 3/3/0/3). The owner approved both changes October 2, 2026. Confidence 0.8. Plastic, run and wear differences remain; the reviewer average pools those effects and is not a measurement. Sources read October 2, 2026.

overrides.adjustmentNote: Latitude 64 and the Atlas baseline list Trident at 6/4/-0.5/3. Atlas moves fade half a step (3 to 3.5); speed 6, glide 4 and the existing turn -0.5 stay unchanged. Infinite Discs' reviewer-average fade is 3.9 (50 reviews), with an Opto average of 3.8 (17 reviews). Batch-5 research records Latitude 64's monster hooking fade description and says every readable reviewer comment supports a stronger finish, with none contradicting; the current Opto page also describes a forceful hook. Counter-evidence: printed manufacturer fade remains 3. The supporting reviews are anonymous pooled reports with no arm speeds stated; the Opto subset is not independent of the overall pool. The owner approved fade 3 to 3.5 on October 2, 2026. Confidence 0.65. Plastic, run and wear effects remain; no plastic-specific ratings were averaged into this mold-level estimate.

overrides.adjustmentNote: Atlas corrects the legacy Gator rating 5/2/0/3 to Innova's current 5/2/0/4: fade 3 to 4, with speed 5, glide 2 and turn 0 unchanged. Innova's factory store and innovadiscs.com disc archive both print 5/2/0/4, spot-checked October 2, 2026. Titan, Foundation Discs and Disc Golf Dojo also list 5/2/0/4. Innova's related Caiman, derived from the Gator, lists 5.5/2/0/4. Counter-evidence: the Atlas baseline, Marshall Street, Infinite's listing and DiscMetrics still show fade 3, consistent with catalog lag. Infinite's reviewer-average fade 3.1-3.2 is discounted because it may be anchored on the displayed 3; that explanation is an inference, not a measured bias. The owner approved fade 3 to 4 on October 2, 2026. Confidence 0.7. This is a manufacturer-number correction, not an average across plastics. Gator3 remains 5/2/0/3 because its Innova page returned 404 during batch research and its rating could not be confirmed; Caiman is unchanged.

overrides.adjustmentNote: Dynamic Discs publishes Trespass at 12/5/-0.5/3. Atlas moves turn half a step (-0.5 to -1); speed 12, glide 5 and fade 3 stay unchanged. The supplied batch-8 research records Infinite Discs reviewer-average turn -1.1 on the whole-mold page (177 ratings), Lucid (71) and Fuzion (38). Lucid and Fuzion are premium plastics. All three averages move away from the displayed -0.5 toward more turn, so simple agreement with the displayed rating cannot explain the direction; this does not measure or eliminate every possible review bias. Reviewers in the batch-8 sample report throwing distances of 300-400+ ft and compare Trespass with Wraith and Destroyer flights. Counter-evidence: the manufacturer still prints -0.5; the overall average pools plastics, and the plastic-specific subsets overlap the overall pool rather than providing three independent samples. DGCR threads were unreadable. The owner approved turn -0.5 to -1 on October 3, 2026. Confidence 0.65. No cross-plastic averaging was performed, and plastic, run, weight and wear differences remain. Wraith and Destroyer are unchanged; review them together with Trespass if its rating moves again.

overrides.consensusNote: The supplied whole-mold, Lucid and Fuzion reviewer averages each give turn -1.1 despite displayed -0.5. Agreement across the premium-plastic subsets supports a conservative mold-level turn -1, while the manufacturer remains at -0.5. Movement away from the displayed number argues against simple display anchoring; pooled averages and overlapping samples still limit confidence. Wraith and Destroyer must be reviewed together with Trespass if it moves again; neither changes now.
overrides.plasticVariance: Lucid and Fuzion are the premium-plastic reference signals, each with reviewer-average turn -1.1; they were not averaged together or with other plastics. The whole-mold pool includes multiple plastics, runs, weights and wear states, and overlaps both subsets. These are coarse reviewer signals, not controlled measurements or plastic-specific ratings.
